g1|variants|subscription billing.family_title: Subscription Billing Integration with SAP S/4HANA OTC
g1|variants|subscription billing.summary: This scenario family covers the integration between subscription management solutions (such as SAP Subscription Billing or SAP Convergent Charging) and S/4HANA Order-to-Cash for recurring revenue processing. Variants differ by whether billing is performed externally with pass-through billing documents, or internally via converged billing contracts leading to SD billing.

variants.name: External Subscription Billing via Convergent Invoicing (FICA)
variants.when_used: When subscriptions are managed in SAP Subscription Billing, replicated via SAP Subscription Billing integration, and billed via Convergent Invoicing before creating FI-CA/FI-AR postings.
variants.key_config: Activation of Convergent Invoicing integration, Provider Contract maintenance in FI-CA, mapping of external billing items to Convergent Invoicing item types.

variants.name: Subscription Order with SD Billing (Convergent Billing)
variants.when_used: When subscription orders are captured natively in S/4HANA SD as provider contracts, utilizing SD billing and invoicing plans for recurring billing cycles.
variants.key_config: Configuration of Provider Contract item categories, billing plans with date rules, and integration with Convergent Charging for usage-based rating.

variants.name: Usage-Based Metered Billing via Convergent Charging (CC)
variants.when_used: When consumption data is rated in SAP Convergent Charging and transferred to S/4HANA for billing and invoicing execution.
variants.key_config: Setup of rating hierarchies, charge plan mapping, consumption item mapping (CIT) in Convergent Invoicing, and billable item (BIT) management.

g1|core|subscription billing|external su.title: External Subscription Billing via Convergent Invoicing (FICA)
g1|core|subscription billing|external su.story: Think of this as a magic subscription box that arrives every month because you signed up online, and the system automatically charges your credit card and sends the invoice without anyone lifting a finger. Technically, this standard SAP S/4HANA Order-to-Cash (OTC) integration scenario ingests external subscription data from SAP Subscription Billing via SAP Cloud Integration (CI) APIs, processes sales orders using item category TAS (Third-Party / Subscription) and schedule line category CS, creates Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable (FI-CA) billing documents, and posts convergent invoices for downstream financial settlement.
g1|core|subscription billing|external su.why_business_needs_it: Modern subscription businesses require automated, high-volume recurring billing and usage-based monetization that traditional SD billing cannot handle natively. Integrating external subscription management with Convergent Invoicing ensures seamless order capture, accurate periodic invoicing, and robust revenue recognition without manual intervention.

g1|core|subscription billing|subscriptio.title: Subscription Order with SD Billing (Convergent Billing)
g1|core|subscription billing|subscriptio.story: Just like a monthly toy box subscription where you get new toys delivered every month and billed automatically, SAP sets up recurring sales orders so the system creates orders and invoices on a regular schedule. In SAP S/4HANA, the subscription order uses provider contracts and specific item categories to manage recurring billing through standard Sales and Distribution (SD) invoicing.
g1|core|subscription billing|subscriptio.why_business_needs_it: Subscription business models generate predictable, recurring revenue streams while automating periodic billing cycles for services or physical goods. It links recurring sales contracts directly to standard SD billing to ensure seamless customer invoicing and financial postings without manual intervention.

modules.role: Manages the subscription order entry, provider contract creation, item category determination, and standard SD billing generation.
modules.hands_off_to: FI-AR (Financial Accounting - Accounts Receivable) for customer invoice posting and revenue recognition.

modules.role: Receives the SD billing document and posts the open item to the customer account.

config_steps.step: Define Subscription Order Document Type CMOV
config_steps.where: VOV8 -- SPRO > Sales and Distribution > Sales Documents > Sales Document Header > Define Sales Document Types
config_steps.values: Sales Document Type CMOV configured with internal number range 01 and item increment 10.
config_steps.check: Run transaction SE16N for table TVAK and verify entry CMOV exists.
config_steps.why: This step sets up the core sales document header control so the system knows how to process subscription orders.
config_steps.if_missing: Without document type CMOV, the system cannot create subscription orders and throws message V1002.
actions: Enter /nVOV8 in the command field and press Enter
Select standard sales document type OR and click Copy As (F6)
Overwrite Sales Doc. Type with CMOV and Description with "Subscription Order"
Set Number range internal to 01 and Number range external to 02
Set Item numbering increment to 10 and Subitem increment to 10
Ensure Signoff check is selected
Save (Ctrl+S) and assign a customizing transport request

config_steps.step: Define Item Category for Subscription CBX1
config_steps.where: VOV7 -- SPRO > Sales and Distribution > Sales Documents > Sales Document Items > Define Item Categories
config_steps.values: Item Category CBX1 created with billing relevance B for order-related billing.
config_steps.check: Run transaction SE16N for table TVAP and verify entry CBX1 exists.
config_steps.why: This step defines how individual subscription items behave regarding pricing and billing schedules.
config_steps.if_missing: If item category CBX1 is missing, subscription orders cannot determine pricing or billing relevance, triggering message V1311.
actions: Enter /nVOV7 in the command field and press Enter
Select standard item category TAN and click Copy As (F6)
Overwrite Item Category with CBX1 and Description with "Subscription Item"
Set Item Type to Standard
Set Billing relevance to B (Order-related billing - based on order quantity)
Set Pricing to X (Standard pricing)
Save (Ctrl+S) and assign transport request

config_steps.step: Assign Item Categories for Document Type CMOV
config_steps.where: VOV4 -- SPRO > Sales and Distribution > Sales Documents > Sales Document Items > Assign Item Categories
config_steps.values: Sales Document Type CMOV and Item Category Group NORM assigned to Item Category CBX1.
config_steps.check: Run SE16N on table TVAPZ and verify combination CMOV / NORM / CBX1.
config_steps.why: This step ensures the system automatically picks the correct subscription item category when you enter a subscription material.
config_steps.if_missing: Without this assignment, entering a subscription material on order CMOV results in error message V1301.
actions: Enter /nVOV4 in the command field and press Enter
Click New Entries
Enter Sales Doc. Type CMOV, Item Category Group NORM, Higher Level Item Cat as blank
Set Default Item Category to CBX1
Save (Ctrl+S) and assign transport request

config_steps.step: Define Billing Document Types for SD Invoicing
config_steps.where: VOFA -- SPRO > Sales and Distribution > Billing > Billing Documents > Define Billing Types
config_steps.values: Billing Type F2 configured with number range 01 and FI posting RVCH.
config_steps.check: Run SE16N on table TVFK and verify billing type F2 parameters.
config_steps.why: This step establishes the billing document rules required to invoice recurring subscription charges.
config_steps.if_missing: Without proper billing type setup, running VF01 for recurring invoices fails with message VF001.
actions: Enter /nVOFA in the command field and press Enter
Select standard billing type F2 and click Copy As (F6)
Verify Billing Type is F2 (or create ZF2 if custom required, using F2 as base)
Set Number range to 01
Set Cancellation billing type to S1
Set Posting to FI to RVCH
Save (Ctrl+S) and assign transport request

config_steps.step: Assign Delivery and Billing Parameters for Document Type CMOV
config_steps.where: VOV8 -- SPRO > Sales and Distribution > Sales Documents > Sales Document Header > Define Sales Document Types
config_steps.values: Delivery type LF and billing type F2 assigned to subscription order CMOV.
config_steps.check: Create a test subscription order CMOV and verify header defaults point to delivery LF and billing F2.
config_steps.why: This step links the subscription order to the correct delivery and billing workflows for order-to-cash execution.
config_steps.if_missing: If billing and delivery types are missing on CMOV, downstream delivery creation (VL01N) or billing (VF01) throws message VL001.
actions: Enter /nVOV8 in the command field and press Enter
Select entry CMOV and click Details
In the Shipping section, set Dlv.type to LF
Ensure Dlv.block is blank

Enter Sales Org 1000, Dist. Channel 10

g1|panel|subscription billing.otc_impact: Subscription billing sits at the intersection of recurring revenue generation and downstream order-to-cash execution, transforming traditional one-off sales orders into recurring billing schedules managed via Convergent Invoicing (FI-CA) or SD billing. It changes order management by introducing recurring billing plans, alters billing output through consumption-based and recurring items, and accelerates cash application through automated recurring invoicing while directly impacting DSO and recurring revenue leakage metrics.

panel_qa.question: How do we decide between using standard SD billing versus Convergent Invoicing (FI-CA) for our subscription models?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Subscription billing requires careful evaluation of volume and complexity, leading to the selection of Convergent Invoicing (FI-CA) for high-volume, event-based metering, or SD billing for straightforward recurring fee schedules. SAP is configured this way because SD billing handles standard sales orders and billing documents directly, whereas Convergent Invoicing (FI-CA) processes high-volume item aggregation through billing master data and billing plans. Key configuration involves assigning billing types (e.g., F2 for SD billing) or configuring Convergent Invoicing contract accounts and provider contracts in transaction FPCJ and FP01. The leadership value lies in aligning system architecture with transaction volume to prevent performance bottlenecks and reduce total cost of ownership. Moving forward, we evaluate usage scaling to determine the right billing engine for upcoming product launches. The weak answer to avoid is suggesting we use SD billing for millions of real-time usage records without considering performance limits.
panel_qa.trap: Suggesting SD billing for millions of real-time usage records without considering performance limits.

panel_qa.question: What is the end-to-end integration flow when usage data comes from Convergent Charging into Order-to-Cash?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: External usage metering requires seamless hand-offs from Convergent Charging (CC) through Convergent Invoicing (FI-CA) to generate billing documents that ultimately post to Financial Accounting (FI). SAP is configured this way because rating and charging engines handle massive event streams that standard Sales and Distribution (SD) tables cannot efficiently store. Key configuration requires setting up the Convergent Charging integration framework via RFC destinations, maintaining rating areas, and mapping consumption items (CIT) to billing items (BIT) in Convergent Invoicing. The leadership value is ensuring accurate, real-time revenue recognition and zero revenue leakage from unrated usage events. Next, we validate the end-to-end IDoc or Web Service message flow during integration testing. The weak answer to avoid is stating that usage data flows directly from Convergent Charging into standard SD billing tables without intermediate aggregation.
panel_qa.trap: Stating that usage data flows directly from Convergent Charging into standard SD billing tables without intermediate aggregation.

panel_qa.question: How does recurring subscription billing impact our Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) and cash application efficiency?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Recurring billing automates the generation of invoices on predefined billing dates, significantly reducing manual billing effort and accelerating customer payment cycles. SAP is configured this way because billing plans attached to subscription orders trigger billing creation automatically via background jobs, feeding clean receivables directly into FI-CA or FI-AR. Key configuration involves defining billing plan types in IMG path Sales and Distribution > Basic Functions > Billing Plan, and setting up automatic clearing rules in transaction FP32 for FI-CA. The leadership value is lower DSO, improved cash flow predictability, and reduced administrative overhead in the billing department. Next, we monitor billing block resolution rates and automated clearing ratios on our executive dashboard. The weak answer to avoid is claiming that subscription billing eliminates the need for credit management and dunning procedures.
panel_qa.trap: Claiming that subscription billing eliminates the need for credit management and dunning procedures.

panel_qa.question: How do we handle mid-term subscription changes, such as upgrades, downgrades, or cancellations, in the sales order?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Mid-term contract modifications require subscription order change processes that update provider contracts and recalculate recurring or usage fees prospectively. SAP is configured this way because standard sales order change routines must synchronize with Convergent Invoicing provider contract change APIs to adjust billing schedules correctly. Key configuration involves maintaining subscription item categories with item category group SBN1 and activating contract change control in Customizing for Service / Subscription Management. The leadership value is maintaining accurate customer billing records and preventing customer disputes caused by erroneous proration calculations. Next, we will audit contract change logs to verify prorated billing accuracy. The weak answer to avoid is saying we delete and recreate subscription orders whenever a customer modifies their service tier.
panel_qa.trap: Saying we delete and recreate subscription orders whenever a customer modifies their service tier.

panel_qa.question: What governance controls are in place to prevent duplicate billing runs and ensure rating accuracy for high-volume subscriptions?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: High-volume subscription processing requires strict job scheduling controls and rating verification checks to prevent duplicate invoicing and unbilled usage gaps. SAP is configured this way because Convergent Invoicing uses mass run transaction groups (e.g., FKKBIX01 for billing and FKKINV_C for invoicing) that process data in parallel threads with built-in reconciliation. Key configuration involves setting run date and identification parameters in transaction FPCJ alongside authorization group restrictions. The leadership value is financial compliance, audit readiness, and protection against revenue loss from skipped rating cycles. Next, we implement automated alert monitoring for failed mass run jobs using SAP Solution Manager. The weak answer to avoid is assuming the system inherently prevents concurrent execution of the same billing mass run without scheduling locks.
panel_qa.trap: Assuming the system inherently prevents concurrent execution of the same billing mass run without scheduling locks.

panel_qa.question: How do deferred revenue and revenue recognition comply with accounting standards (IFRS 15) in subscription billing scenarios?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Subscription contracts often bundle upfront fees, recurring charges, and usage-based components that must be allocated and recognized over time using Revenue Accounting and Reporting (RAR). SAP is configured this way because SD billing or Convergent Invoicing documents pass performance obligations and pricing elements to RAR for allocation based on standalone selling prices. Key configuration involves integrating SD billing types with RAR via transaction FARR_CUST and defining fulfillment types for subscription items. The leadership value is strict compliance with statutory accounting regulations and transparent financial reporting. Next, we review monthly RAR contract liability and revenue posting reports. The weak answer to avoid is stating that revenue is always recognized entirely on the billing document date regardless of service delivery periods.
panel_qa.trap: Stating that revenue is always recognized entirely on the billing document date regardless of service delivery periods.

g1|core|subscription billing|usage-based.title: Usage-Based Metered Billing via Convergent Charging (CC)
g1|core|subscription billing|usage-based.story: Just like a water meter tracks every drop you use and charges you only for what you consumed, this process measures how much of a service you use and bills you for it. Precisely, usage data from SAP Convergent Charging flows through Web Services APIs into Sales and Distribution usage items, triggering Convergent Invoicing billing documents and event-based revenue recognition.
g1|core|subscription billing|usage-based.why_business_needs_it: Subscription businesses require accurate, automated billing based on actual consumption metrics to monetize digital services and usage-based products effectively. This ensures correct revenue accounting and eliminates manual usage data collection.
